injected_codes.rationale: The provided solver code has multiple failure modes causing "list index out of range": (1) the makespan function assumes m >= 1 and n >= 1 when indexing C[0][j], C[i][0], C[i][j-1] etc. without guards, (2) for n=0 the early return exists but the judge likely still invokes makespan on empty seq leading to C = [] then C[0][j] access, (3) for n=1 the hardcoded [1] works but the surrounding logic doesn't generalize, and (4) the insertion loop builds permutations but doesn't protect against malformed seq (duplicates or wrong length) that the judge's C matrix can index into. The NEH-style insertion (sort by total time + greedy best-position insertion) is directionally correct but the heuristic only reaches ~0.3 at best on larger instances, far below the 0.795 known optimum, so the gap is structural. Highest-impact fix is to inject a battle-tested, edge-case-safe makespan helper into solver_lib (the solver cannot reliably write this from scratch due to the off-by-one and missing guards); pre_process adds task-structure guidance so the solver conditions its insertion loop on n/m bounds and uses the helper. This targets the exact failure pattern without overhauling the existing heuristic.
